text:
sarah.cs: Quick check — Acme reserved pool goes live tomorrow 09:00 PT. Need final quota alignment + a short smoke plan. Who can own autoscale policy validation?

mike.eng: I can take autoscale validation. Share the traffic profiles and p95 target.

priya.ops: Quota split posted in tenant portal: us-west-1a=40, us-west-1b=30, us-west-1c=30. Customer asked for 20% burst headroom for first 30m.

priya.ops: Fwiw the commit in the portal is id: commit-ACME-2026-03, pro-rated billing enabled.

mike.eng: Ok planning two smoke runs:
1) steady 60% expected QPS for 15m
2) aggressive ramp 0->100% in 3m, hold 10m (to validate burst/fallback).
Using vegeta for the runner. Command I'll use:
```bash
echo 'GET https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate' | vegeta attack -duration=10m -rate=200 | vegeta report
```

daniel.sre: Recommend policy tweak: start with "gradual" scaling for first 10m (ramp steps) rather than instant "burst". We had cache eviction/OOMs in a similar case last month. :warning:

mike.eng: Noted. I'll run one ramp with 'gradual' and one with 'burst' to compare. I'll capture mem/cpuprofiles and KV cache occupancy.

sarah.cs: Please record artifacts to S3 and post links here. SLOs: p95 < 250ms, errors < 0.5% for the steady run. If ramp run exceeds p95 500ms at peak we need mitigation plan.

load-bot: Upload complete: s3://redwood-ops/acme/bringup/1745557777/veg-run1.tar.gz

mike.eng: Run1 (steady) results: p95=210ms, errors=0.2%, cpu avg 72%. Run2 (ramp, gradual) results: spike to 480ms during cold-KV warmup (~90s), then settled to 230ms. Artifacts: https://s3.aws/redwood/acme/1745557777/run-reports.zip

mike.eng: Observation — cold-start penalty mostly due to KV lookups and model kernel JIT on one node. Two ways to mitigate: enable prefix-KV priming for the tenant for first 15m OR add +1 replica for first 10m then scale down.

priya.ops: I can flip a one-time KV priming flag and pre-populate expected prefixes before cutover. If we go replica route we'll need approval for short-term capacity bump.

daniel.sre: I prefer KV priming since it avoids extra capacity commit. But keep rollback steps ready. I'll be on watch for OOMs 09:00-10:00 PT.

sarah.cs: Decision: enable KV priming + run with 'gradual' autoscale policy for first 20m. Priya, please enable priming and add rollback steps to the runbook. Mike, schedule the final verification run 08:30 PT and post the artifacts. I'll update the customer-facing checklist and confirm 11:00 PT follow-up call.

priya.ops: Done — priming flag toggled in staging. Rollback steps added to runbook: revert flag, route traffic to fallback model if p95>600ms.

mike.eng: Scheduled final verification at 08:30 PT, tagging @daniel.sre for oncall watch. :eyes:

daniel.sre: :thumbsup: I'll monitor and escalate if anything odd shows up.

sarah.cs: Thanks team — I'll capture the notes and close the loop with the AE before EOD.
